skill.name: feature-dev-complete
skill.description: Coordinate a complete feature development workflow from research and architecture through implementation, testing, documentation, and pull request preparation.
skill.summary: Coordinates a 12-stage feature delivery workflow using Claude, Codex, Gemini, testing, documentation, and release checks.
skill.author: DNYoussef

security_audit.summary: Most static hits are false positives from Markdown fences, inline command names, and fixed local report parsing in an example shell workflow. The skill still carries meaningful risk because it instructs users or agents to run external AI tools, automate source changes, and create commits or pull requests.

remediation.issue: Autonomous source changes and pull request creation
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before copying generated files, running git add or git commit, or creating a GitHub pull request. Default pull request creation to off.

remediation.issue: External AI tools receive feature and codebase context
remediation.suggestion: Document which tools receive repository content and require consent before using Gemini or Codex with target directories or generated context files.

remediation.issue: Executable shell workflow embedded in documentation
remediation.suggestion: Convert the long bash block into reviewed pseudocode or split it into guarded steps with prerequisites, dry-run mode, and rollback guidance.

semantic_findings.title: Autonomous Repository Modification and Pull Request Creation
semantic_findings.description: The workflow asks Codex to run in full-auto mode, then copies generated implementation files into the target directory and creates a git commit and GitHub pull request. A user who follows the skill could allow broad automated source changes and repository publication without enough human approval.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited lines directly invoke full-auto Codex, copy implementation output into the target tree, run git add and commit, and call gh pr create. The behavior is explicit and not inferred from naming alone.

semantic_findings.description: The workflow sends feature details and repository context to Gemini and Codex tooling, including a target directory passed through a files option. This can expose proprietary code or design details to external model services unless users give explicit consent.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The workflow explicitly calls Gemini with a files option for the target directory and calls Codex with generated context files. The exact service transport depends on the tools, so confidence is high but not absolute.

content.value_statement: Complex feature work can stall when research, architecture, implementation, testing, and documentation are handled separately. This skill coordinates a staged workflow that guides Claude, Codex, and Gemini through delivery checks.
actual_capabilities: Defines a 12-stage workflow from research through deployment readiness.
Assigns roles to Gemini, Claude, Codex, and related workflow commands.
Specifies artifacts for research, architecture, diagrams, implementation, tests, documentation, and quality reports.
Includes quality gates for test status, quality score, and critical security issues.
Documents integration points with related cascades, commands, and skills.
limitations: Requires external tools such as Gemini, Codex, npx, jq, git, and gh.
The main workflow is documented as shell script text, not packaged executable code.
Full automation can modify repository files and create commits or pull requests.
The codebase size check focuses on JavaScript and TypeScript files.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Product Feature
use_cases.description: Turn a feature request into research notes, architecture direction, implementation tasks, and quality gates.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Implementation Work
use_cases.description: Use a staged process to prototype, test, polish, and document a feature before review.

use_cases.title: Prepare Release Evidence
use_cases.description: Collect test, style, security, documentation, and readiness outputs for a pull request review.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Feature Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a scoped feature workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to plan the feature: [describe the feature]. Keep the target directory unchanged until I approve implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Design Before Building
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for research and architecture first.
prompt_templates.prompt: Research current best practices for [feature], analyze existing patterns in [directory], and draft an architecture plan with risks and test strategy.

prompt_templates.title: Run Guarded Implementation
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for implementation with review gates.
prompt_templates.prompt: Implement [feature] in [directory] using staged checkpoints. Ask before file copy, git operations, external service calls, or pull request creation.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Review Package
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a release readiness package for [feature] with test results, quality findings, security review notes, documentation changes, and unresolved decisions.

output_examples.input: Add user authentication with refresh tokens to a web application.
output: Research summary covering current authentication practices.
Architecture plan with data flow and risk notes.
Implementation and test checklist with readiness gates.
Pull request preparation notes for reviewer handoff.

output_examples.input: Prepare a payment integration feature for review.
output: Feature delivery plan organized by research, architecture, build, testing, security, and documentation stages.
Quality evidence summary with tests, style review, and security scan outcomes.
Open decisions and manual approval points before repository changes.

output_examples.input: Improve an existing dark mode feature and document release readiness.
output_examples.output: A concise readiness report with implementation status, testing evidence, documentation updates, and deployment blockers.

best_practices: Run the workflow on a branch or disposable workspace before touching production code.
Review research, architecture, and generated changes before allowing commit or pull request steps.
Confirm external model usage is acceptable before sending repository context to AI services.
anti_patterns: Do not enable full automation in a repository that contains uncommitted or sensitive work.
Do not skip the security and quality gates just to create a faster pull request.
Do not use this workflow when the feature scope or target directory is unclear.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It guides a complete feature delivery workflow from research and architecture to testing, documentation, and pull request preparation.

faq.question: Does it write code by itself?
faq.answer: The documented workflow can call Codex for implementation, but users should approve file changes before they are copied into the project.

faq.question: Which tools does it expect?
faq.answer: It references Claude, Codex, Gemini, npx claude-flow commands, jq, git, and the GitHub CLI.

faq.question: Can it create a pull request?
faq.answer: Yes, the workflow includes a pull request step when enabled. Review generated changes before allowing that step.

faq.question: Is it limited to one framework?
faq.answer: No framework is required, but the included line-count analysis focuses on JavaScript and TypeScript files.

faq.question: How should teams use it safely?
faq.answer: Use a separate branch, confirm external tool permissions, review generated changes, and keep manual approval gates for repository writes.
